subject: Hardware profiles rollout: risk posture + oncall readiness (canary/rollback criteria)
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 8:12 AM
Subject: Hardware profiles rollout: risk posture + oncall readiness (canary/rollback criteria)

Ava,

Before we move beyond limited canary for the hardware tuning profiles pack (H100/L40S now; B200 gated), SRE needs the rollout to meet a minimum oncall-readiness bar. We’re already seeing customer sensitivity around latency shifts tied to “runtime config updates” (see SUP-29410).

Asks (need written agreement + links in the runbook):

1) Explicit rollback criteria (objective, not “looks good”)
- Latency: rollback if p95 end-to-end latency worsens >8% vs control for >15 min at same traffic mix (segment streaming vs non-streaming).
- Tail spikes: rollback if p99 increases >12% for >10 min OR if we see new bimodal behavior in the latency histogram.
- Errors: rollback if 5xx rate increases by >0.15% absolute OR if retry rate increases by >0.3% absolute.
- Capacity/throughput: rollback if tokens/sec per GPU drops >5% sustained (we can accept short dips during cache warmup).
- OOM/evictions: rollback if OOM events are non-zero for H100 pools (should be 0) or if L40S OOM increases above baseline by >0.05% of requests.

2) A fast “kill switch” that oncall can flip per pool/region
- Must not require a code deploy.
- Must take effect within 10 minutes (config propagation + process restart plan if required).
- Must be documented as step 1 in the incident playbook.

3) Dashboards + alert routing must be in place before ramp
- A single rollout view: profile selection breakdown, override source, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU mem/KV cache headroom, 5xx/retries.
- Alerts must page eng-oncall for profile regressions (not just Slack).

Proposed canonical docs (please confirm these are the sources of truth and up to date):
- Rollout runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSERVE/Rollout+Runbook+-+Hardware+Tuning+Profiles
- Perf canary gates: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPLAT/Perf+Canary+Gates+for+Hardware+Profiles
- Rollout dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/runtime-profile-rollout/hardware-profiles-rollout-overview
- Runtime SLO dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/runtime-slo/serving-runtime-slo-latency-and-errors

If you want to waive any of the thresholds above for business reasons, we should do it explicitly and time-box it (and accept the paging/incident risk). Otherwise SRE is going to ask Release to keep ramp capped.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Reliability / SRE Sponsor
Redwood Inference


On Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 9:03 AM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 9:03 AM
Subject: Re: Hardware profiles rollout: risk posture + oncall readiness (canary/rollback criteria)

Thanks. Agree on the need for objective rollback.

Two questions:
1) Are we comfortable with different thresholds per SKU? L40S is inherently tighter on memory and I don’t want us to thrash on small, expected variance.
2) Can we treat the first 24h as “learning” and page only if hard errors (5xx/OOM), while we tune the noise in p99?

If we can align today, I’ll ask the teams to update the runbook and gate the ramp behind SRE sign-off.

Ava

—
Ava Chen
Engineering Leadership
Redwood Inference


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 10:21 AM
Subject: Re: Hardware profiles rollout: risk posture + oncall readiness (canary/rollback criteria)

On SKU-specific thresholds: yes, but only if they’re written down and tied to the workload envelope (streaming/non-streaming, seq length buckets, concurrency) so oncall isn’t guessing.

Concrete proposal:
- H100: keep the thresholds as stated (it’s the “premium” pool where customers have strict SLO expectations).
- L40S: allow 10% p95 / 15% p99 variance *only* when queue depth remains below the backpressure limit and 5xx/retries are flat. Still hard-stop on any OOM regression.

On “learning period”: I’m ok with reduced paging for p99 for the first 24h *only* if:
- We still page for 5xx/retries/OOM/tokens/sec drops.
- We still alert (non-paging) for p95/p99 drift so the team sees it in real time.
- The canary is capped (e.g., <=5% traffic per pool) until we exit learning mode.

Also: please make sure the dashboard includes “selected_profile” and “override_source” broken out by pool. Without that, we burn hours correlating.

I think the metrics work is in flight (PR mentioned in weekly notes), but I need the link and expected metric names in the runbook.

Neha


On Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 12:06 PM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 12:06 PM
Subject: Re: Hardware profiles rollout: risk posture + oncall readiness (canary/rollback criteria)

This is reasonable.

Action items I’m taking back to the teams today:
- Update rollout runbook with the SKU-specific thresholds and the 24h learning mode rules.
- Ensure we have a per-pool kill switch documented as the first rollback step.
- Confirm the profile selection metrics land and are on the rollout dashboard.

For reference, the two implementation items I’ve seen in review/merge queue:
- Profile selection metrics/debug endpoint (for selected_profile + override source): PR redwood/pr-22027
- Canary gates update: PR perf-canary/pr-731

I’ll reply again once the runbook is updated with final links and we can treat that as the SRE sign-off artifact.

Ava


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 2:47 PM
Subject: Re: Hardware profiles rollout: risk posture + oncall readiness (canary/rollback criteria)

Perfect.

One more requirement to avoid repeating SUP-29410:
- When we flip canary on for a pool, we need a single changelog entry with timestamp + profile version + runtime version, and it must be visible to oncall (either in the rollout dashboard annotations or in the deploy notes). Otherwise we can’t answer “what changed?” fast enough during customer escalations.

If that’s covered in the runbook update, SRE will sign off for the next ramp step.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Reliability / SRE Sponsor
Redwood Inference
